questions.question: Find the surface area of a closed box 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm and of a triangular prism with 3, 4, 5 cm right-angled ends and length 10 cm. State the general prism formula you used.
questions.expected_answer: Box: 2(lb + lh + bh) = 2(12 + 8 + 6) = 2 × 26 = 52 cm². Prism: each end has area ½ × 3 × 4 = 6, so the two ends give 12 cm²; the three rectangles 3 × 10, 4 × 10 and 5 × 10 give 30 + 40 + 50 = 120 cm², which is the perimeter 12 times the length 10. Total 12 + 120 = 132 cm². General formula: surface area = 2 × area of end + perimeter of end × length.

questions.question: A closed tin has radius 3.5 cm and height 10 cm. Find its total surface area, the area of its label, and its volume and capacity. Explain where 2πrh comes from.
questions.expected_answer: Ends: 2 × π × 3.5² ≈ 76.97 cm². Label (curved surface): 2 × π × 3.5 × 10 ≈ 219.91 cm². Total ≈ 296.88 cm². Volume: π × 3.5² × 10 ≈ 384.85 cm³, so the capacity is about 385 ml since 1 cm³ holds 1 ml. 2πrh is the area of the label unrolled into a rectangle: its length is the circumference 2πr and its breadth is the height h.

questions.question: A crate measures 1.2 m by 80 cm by 50 cm. Find its volume in cubic centimetres, litres and cubic metres, and explain why 1 m³ is 1 000 000 cm³ and not 100 cm³.
questions.expected_answer: Convert first: 120 cm by 80 cm by 50 cm. Volume 120 × 80 × 50 = 480 000 cm³. Litres: 480 000 ÷ 1 000 = 480 litres. Cubic metres: 480 000 ÷ 1 000 000 = 0.48 m³. A cube 1 m on each side is 100 cm long, 100 cm wide and 100 cm high, so it holds 100 × 100 × 100 = 1 000 000 cubes of 1 cm³; the factor 100 applies once for each of the three dimensions.
